title: Deleep Singh v. District Magistrate
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner relegated to Clause 6.8 objection.
headnote: Writ seeking quashing of a recovery certificate as contrary to Section 56 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 8.2 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 disposed of without merits on the licensee's statement that the consumer may file an objection under Clause 6.8, to be decided by a reasoned speaking order after hearing.
facts: Deleep Singh filed a writ in the Allahabad High Court to quash a recovery certificate or writ of demand dated 14 March 2022, saying it was issued without authority and contrary to Section 56 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 8.2 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Respondents included the District Magistrate and the electricity licensee (respondent no.3). Licensee's counsel stated on instructions that the petitioner could file a Paragraph 6.8 objection. The Court did not examine the demand on merits.

holding_units.topic: objection to recovery demand — alternate remedy
holding_units.holding: Where the licensee states that the consumer may file an objection under Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 against a recovery certificate or writ of demand, the High Court may dispose of a writ challenging that demand without expressing any opinion on merits, directing that any such objection filed within four weeks be decided by a reasoned speaking order, preferably within four weeks, after reasonable opportunity of hearing.

principle_tags.application: Writ against a recovery certificate disposed of by relegating the petitioner to a Clause 6.8 objection, without a merits grant or refusal.
On the licensee's statement, the Court directed that a Paragraph 6.8 objection, if filed within four weeks, be decided by a reasoned speaking order after hearing.
